sections.blurb: Recognisable structures that need distinctive steps.

sections.title: Basics
sections.blurb: Simple builds used to check the controller and the breakage model.

dog.title: Dog
dog.description: Ten bricks: four legs, a wide body bridging them, a neck, head and tail.
dog.tests: wide bricks bridging legs; ten-brick figure

bridge.title: Arch bridge
bridge.description: A corbel arch: each pier steps one stud inward, then a 2x10 deck closes the arch by landing on both piers. Two parapets finish the deck.
bridge.tests: a deck landing on two piers (corbel arch)

house.title: House
house.description: A facade with a doorway. Two walls stand two courses high, a 2x10 lintel spans the door and lands on both walls, and a stepped gable roof and a chimney finish it.
house.tests: a lintel over a doorway; stepped roof
house.mechanism: B: release load on an 8-stud wall joint
house.needs: ease off 0.5 mm before letting go

press 0.2 mm below seated, no easing off (controller default)
0.5 s gripper release, no easing off (controller default)

log_cabin.title: Log cabin
log_cabin.description: Courses alternate direction, and every brick above the first interlocks two corners below. It is planned on one corner and lands on both.

locomotive.title: Steam locomotive
locomotive.description: Three wheels, a 2x10 chassis that rests on all three, a cab under an overhanging roof, a boiler and a smokestack.
locomotive.tests: a chassis resting on three wheels

table_grip.title: Table, grip-aware
table_grip.description: The table's ten bricks, with each grip chosen for room. The legs are gripped across the axis where they are 4 studs apart, and the 2x8 tops are gripped end to end, so no finger enters a 2-stud gap.
